definitions.explanation: The fibrous tissue that forms over a wound after healing. Used as the formal medical term for scars, in contrast to the more everyday word {傷跡|きずあと}.

examples.japanese: {手術後|しゅじゅつご}の{瘢痕|はんこん}が{残|のこ}った。
examples.english: A scar remained after the surgery.

examples.japanese: {瘢痕|はんこん}が{目立|めだ}たなくなるまで{半年|はんとし}かかった。
examples.english: It took half a year for the scar to become less noticeable.

examples.japanese: {火傷|やけど}による{瘢痕|はんこん}を{治療|ちりょう}するために、{形成外科|けいせいげか}を{受診|じゅしん}した。
examples.english: I visited a plastic surgeon to treat the scar from a burn.

notes:
The formal medical term for scar tissue. In everyday conversation, Japanese speakers typically use {傷跡|きずあと} (scar) or {跡|あと} (mark), while {瘢痕|はんこん} is reserved for clinical and written contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {瘢痕|はんこん}{組織|そしき}: scar tissue
- {瘢痕|はんこん}が{残|のこ}る: a scar remains
- {瘢痕|はんこん}{治療|ちりょう}: scar treatment
- {肥厚性|ひこうせい}{瘢痕|はんこん}: hypertrophic scar
- ケロイド{瘢痕|はんこん}: keloid scar

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {傷跡|きずあと}: scar — everyday word for a visible scar on the skin
- {痕|あと}: mark, trace — general word for any mark left behind
- ケロイド: keloid — a specific type of raised, overgrown scar tissue
